newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL - COLTS QUARTERBACK HARBAUGH OUT TWO TO THREE WEEKS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL - COLTS QUARTERBACK HARBAUGH OUT TWO TO THREE WEEKS.

text.p: Indianapolis Colts quarterback Jim Harbaugh is likely to miss two to three weeks with a strained medial collateral ligament in his left knee sustained during a 27-13 loss at New England Sunday.

Harbaugh suffered the injury in the third quarter when New England safety Willie Clay blitzed and rolled up on Harbaugh's knee as he tried to tackle him. Harbaugh completed 11-of-18 passes for 119 yards with an interception before the injury.
"He came down on my knee," said Harbaugh. "I had the long spikes in (on cleats), maybe that contributed. I could feel it buckle, pop a little bit and tear.
"It looks like I'll be about two to three weeks. It was a tough loss and a real setback. We'll probably have to run the table to have a chance" to make the playoffs.

"It looks like a two to three week situation," Colts coach Lindy Infante said. "It probably could be worse, we'll have to wait and see. It never helps to lose one of your starters or star players. I think the team went about its business the best way it could after it happened."

Backup quarterback Paul Justin completed 11-of-22 yards for 128 yards and one touchdown in a relief role. Kerwin Bell is the third-string quarterback for the Colts (6-6), who have lost five of their last six games.
